prompt:
The GAL-TAN framework identifies political orientation on a single axis. Individuals and texts are placed according to the degree to which their views align with either pole, as follows:

  - Individuals at the GAL (Green/Alternative/Libertarian) pole support expanded
    personal freedoms and social liberalisation, for example: access to abortion,
    same-sex marriage, environmental protection, and multiculturalism.

  - Individuals at the TAN (Traditional/Authoritarian/Nationalist) pole prioritise
    order, tradition, and stability, and believe that the state should treat the
    maintenance of national identity as a priority, for example: restrictive
    immigration policy, emphasis on law and order, defence of traditional social
    institutions, and national sovereignty over supranational authority.

A text occupies a position on this axis to the extent that it argues FROM these commitments, not to the extent that it mentions the associated topics:

  - Environmental or immigration policy discussed in administrative or fiscal
    terms does not by itself indicate a position.
  - Nuclear expansion argued for energy security is not GAL.
  - Faster asylum processing argued on humanitarian grounds is not TAN.

The profile below describes the positional priorities of the British electorate.

<profile>
  gal: 0.15
  tan: 0.85
</profile>

Below are two texts.

TEXT_E:
The Conservatives invite Britons to join a new kind of government built on the belief that we’re all in this together. Britain’s challenges—debt, social breakdown, and a discredited politics—won’t be solved by big government, but by a Big Society: responsibility shared by individuals, families, businesses and communities, with power devolved from the centre.

Core values and approach
- Responsibility: sound public finances, personal responsibility, social responsibility.
- Enterprise and aspiration: a modern, greener, innovative economy.
- Society is not the state: decentralise power to people, professionals and places.
- Progressive Conservatism: equal opportunity, fighting poverty and inequality, improving wellbeing by trusting people and reforming the state.

Fix the economy
- Eliminate the bulk of the structural deficit in a Parliament; create the Office for Budget Responsibility; emergency Budget; £6bn immediate waste cuts; public sector pay freeze (protecting the lowest paid); stop Labour’s “jobs tax” (NI rise) by cutting waste.
- Lower and simplify business taxes (cut corporation tax), reduce regulation, make Britain open for business.
- Rebalance toward saving, investment, exports and hi‑tech leadership (back R&D, STEM, Dyson reforms).
- Welfare-to-work: a single, payment-by-results Work Programme; reassess incapacity claims; sanctions for refusing work; help entrepreneurs and SMEs win procurement.
- Managed immigration: annual cap on non‑EU economic migrants; tighter student visas; promote integration.
- Modern infrastructure: begin high-speed rail; better, not bigger, Heathrow; rail reform; superfast broadband without a phone tax; local enterprise partnerships.

Better public services and safer finance
- Empower professionals and users: transparency (publish spending), payment by results, mutuals and co‑ops to run services.
- Banking reform: bank levy; Bank of England to supervise prudentially; curb risky trading; boost SME credit.

Build a greener economy
- Green Investment Bank; carbon price floor; shift taxes toward environmental goals; Green Deal to cut home energy bills; smart grid, offshore wind, CCS; nuclear with no subsidy.

Mend our broken society
- Family-friendly Britain: recognise marriage and civil partnerships in tax; end the couple penalty via welfare reform; council tax freeze; flexible working and shared parental leave; protect childhood from commercial pressures; refocus Sure Start on early intervention; 4,200 more health visitors.
- NHS: protect real-terms funding; patient choice across qualified providers; GP commissioning; scrap non‑clinical targets; publish outcomes; 24/7 urgent care; Cancer Drugs Fund; personal health and care budgets; voluntary insurance option for social care.
- Schools: higher teaching standards and discipline; rigorous curriculum and phonics; technical academies; pupil premium; free schools/expanded academies; protect special schools.

Fight crime and strengthen borders
- Tougher knife sentences; overhaul alcohol licensing; elected police commissioners; cut police paperwork; monthly local crime data; Border Police Force; payment-by-results rehabilitation.

Clean up politics and restore liberties
- Recall MPs; cut number of MPs and ministers’ pay; equalise constituencies; petitions to trigger debates; kill the quango state; radical transparency.
- Protect freedoms: scrap ID cards and databases; curb surveillance and DNA retention; UK Bill of Rights; strengthen data protection.
- Localism: neighbourhood planning, referendums, community right to buy, elected mayors.

Protect the environment
- Conserve habitats, reform fisheries, plant a million trees; honest food labelling; sustainable, high‑welfare farming; science-led badger control for bTB.

Promote our national interest
- National Security Council; succeed in Afghanistan; renew Trident; reform defence procurement; restore the Military Covenant.
- Liberal Conservative foreign policy: champion rights and democracy; strong NATO and US ties; deepen links with India and others; stand firm on Iran; two‑state solution.
- EU: positive but guarded—no more power without a referendum; Sovereignty Bill; repatriate powers on key areas; never join the Euro without a referendum.
- One World Conservatism: honour 0.7% aid by 2013; full transparency and results focus; prioritise the poorest; £500m a year to fight malaria; promote trade-led development.

TEXT_G:
UKIP Manifesto 2010 – Summary (ideological framing retained)

Core mission
- Leave the EU to restore three freedoms: action (sovereign decision-making), resources (keep UK money and cut EU red tape), and people (end rule by unelected EU bodies). Replace the LibLabCon consensus with direct democracy, binding referenda, and real local control.

Economy and tax
- Turbocharge enterprise by simplifying tax: raise the personal allowance to £11,500, merge income tax and Employees’ NI into a single 31% flat rate, and phase out Employers’ NI over five years. Abolish Inheritance Tax when conditions allow.
- Cut the state back to its 1997 size, scrap quangos, and replace VAT with a Local Sales Tax that funds councils; return 50% of business rates to local authorities.
- Repeal up to 120,000 EU rules stifling business; defend the City from harmful EU directives; repatriate financial regulation.
- Restore Bank of England authority, raise bank capital ratios, split retail and investment banking (Glass-Steagall style), and reinstate a “corset” on excessive lending.

Jobs, industry, and skills
- Create one million skilled jobs via long-term national programmes: defence, nuclear power, flood/coastal defences, transport, and prison building—anchoring UK manufacturing.
- Production Enterprise Centres to help SMEs innovate and export.
- Denationalise universities/FE via universal Student/Training Vouchers; scrap EU carbon caps and protect strategic UK firms from predatory takeovers.

Immigration and asylum
- Immediate five-year freeze on permanent immigration; thereafter cap at around 50,000 per year. Leave the EU to regain border control; use time-limited work permits and visas; criminalise overstaying; triple border staff; record all entry/exit.
- No amnesty for illegal immigrants; enforce removals. Reinstate the Primary Purpose Rule; end official multiculturalism; require loyalty undertakings for residents; replace the Human Rights Act and leave the ECHR; tighten asylum with secure centres and first-safe-country rules.

Law, order, and defence
- Victims first: elected Police Boards; “life means life”; double prison places; three-strikes policy; stronger homeowner rights; withdraw from the European Arrest Warrant; youth “boot camps.”
- Increase defence spending by 40%; expand the Army and TA; restore the Navy (including three carriers); strengthen the RAF; back NATO, not EU missions; maintain and renew Trident; cut MoD bureaucracy; improve forces’ pay and care.

Public services
- NHS: no frontline cuts; elected County Health Boards; scrap wasteful tiers; franchise services on fixed budgets; Health Credit Vouchers to enable opting out; restore matrons; free eye tests and dental checks.
- Schools: universal School Vouchers; restore rigour in the three Rs; retain/expand grammar and professional schools; end social engineering; more on-the-job teacher training; elected Education Boards; allow meaningful discipline; support special schools and home education.
- Welfare: replace 70+ benefits with a flat-rate Basic Cash Benefit; allow work up to the personal allowance without penalty; enhance Child Benefit (first three children) and introduce Nursery Vouchers; limit benefits to citizens/residents of 5+ years; “Workfare” for claimants.
- Pensions: non-means-tested £130/week Citizen’s Pension at 65; retarget tax relief; reinstate dividend tax credit; freeze unaffordable public sector schemes; scrap PPF/NEST; avoid an EU pensions trap.

Trade, energy, and environment
- Leave the political EU; pursue a Swiss-style trade deal; reclaim the UK’s WTO seat; lead a Commonwealth Free Trade Area; seek deals with NAFTA/ASEAN; promote real human rights.
- Climate realism: repeal the Climate Change Act; expand nuclear to 50% of electricity; use indigenous coal; oppose uneconomic wind (keep large schemes offshore, market-funded); exit EU carbon schemes; convene a Royal Commission on climate science; fund practical environmental improvements and flood defences; electrify transport.

Infrastructure, housing, constitution, culture
- Transport: invest £3bn/year; build high-speed rail lines; reopen railways; improve roads; fair fuel duty; “Britdisc” for foreign HGVs; oppose Heathrow expansion; build a Thames Estuary hub.
- Housing/planning: tackle demand by controlling immigration; bring empty homes into use; scrap regional quangos/IPC; binding local referenda on major schemes; protect Green Belt via elected Conservators.
- Constitution: Swiss-style initiative and referendum (5% trigger); AV+ voting; elected Police/Health/Education Boards; English-only days at Westminster, with devolved business handled by national MPs; recall powers; abolish regional government; support the monarchy and Church of England.
- Britishness: civic nationalism; oppose multiculturalism/political correctness; protect iconic brands/measures; teach Britain’s contributions; counter extremist Islam (ban burqa/niqab in public buildings, deport radical preachers, reaffirm UK law over sharia); celebrate the Commonwealth; English Parliament; St George’s Day holiday.

Farming, fishing, and community
- Leave the CAP but phase support; promote British produce, ethical labelling, co-ops, and a supermarket ombudsman; review/repeal harmful EU directives.
- Exit the CFP; reclaim a 200nm EEZ; end discards and industrial fishing; rebuild stocks and fleets—returning £2.5bn/year to the UK.
- Protect animal welfare; safeguard Royal Mail/Post Offices; allow designated pub smoking rooms; champion small business.

Judge whether TEXT_E or TEXT_G aligns more closely with this profile.

Respond with a single JSON object and nothing else. Do not wrap it in markdown code fences and do not add commentary before or after it. The object must have exactly these keys, in this order:

{
  "evidence": "<the specific commitments in each text you relied on>",
  "reasoning": "<two sentences connecting that evidence to the verdict>",
  "confidence": "high" | "medium" | "low",
  "winner": "TEXT_E" | "TEXT_G"
}
